_README: Curated aliases. Copy this file to aliases.json in your Engram install dir,
replace the examples with your own nodes, then:
(add --apply to write; without it you get a preview)
An alias is new vocabulary for a node whose real name uses your jargon while
the question uses the asker's words. 'owner contact details' and a node named
'Alice Johnson' share no word, so no amount of ranking finds it; one alias does.
It costs nothing to carry. props is already in the FTS index, embeddings.py
embeds aliases with the name, and the name channel treats each alias as an
alternative name — which makes the node pin-eligible whatever its type.
Rule: no alias repeats a word the node's name already has. That is a ranking
hack, not a vocabulary fix. Keys are node ids; 'name' is checked against the
database before writing, so a spec aimed at the wrong DB is refused, not applied.
Keys starting with _ are ignored, so this block can stay in your own file.
